avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, and the fight against the emerald ash borer and heat islands.

etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to supply and plant 1,374 trees on public land, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The total authorized expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, and the trees are spread across seven boroughs [CM26 0186].

The City is paying $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026 [CM26 0351]. Pierrefonds-Roxboro, for its part, is transferring up to $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants [CA26 29 0062].

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening, instead of the required 40 trees and 25% [CA26 27 0058]. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger [CA26 10 149].

Outremont awards a company the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including trails, water retention and plant installation. The authorized expense reaches $800,416.17, taxes included, funded mainly by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux [CA26 16 0053].

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini excavator with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, to plant trees and green the area in 2026 [CA26 27 0106]. The borough is also setting aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, which will replace, among other things, trees cut down because of the emerald ash borer [CA26 27 0146].

City council approves a 24-month lease, starting May 1, 2026, renting plots in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to operate a transitional nursery there. The total rent is $100 and the property subsidy is estimated at $329,600 [CM26 0859].

aSurveiller.texte: Planting of 855 trees in spring 2027 as part of the second batch of planting contracts.
Watering, maintenance and replacement of planted trees until the end of November 2029.

Progress reports from the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain on July 31 and October 31, 2026, accountability reporting by no later than December 31, 2026, then a summary and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve plantings carried out until November 2026.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.
deneigement.enBref: The City and the boroughs rent machinery with operators for snow clearing, snow loading and spring cleaning, and hire companies to clear snow from public squares and parking lots. Several turnkey snow removal and towing contracts are being extended or awarded for the coming seasons. Some boroughs are also amending their by-laws concerning contractors who clear snow from private land.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives and clean streets, sidewalks and bike paths. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expenditure of $574,920.99, taxes included, for the rental of sweepers and tanker trucks [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal from downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie hires companies for the upkeep, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six public squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending by one year the snow removal services for the Quartier des Spectacles, which include the spreading of abrasives and snow loading [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord pays for the rental of an additional grader and Saint-Léonard draws $200,000 from its surpluses for staff pay and the purchase of abrasives [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offers to have the city council provide, itself, the staff for the snow disposal site during loading operations.

The City is extending by twelve months turnkey snow removal contracts in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, as well as towing contracts and equipment rentals with operators in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Ville-Marie and Anjou are also extending rentals of tractor-loaders and a grader, and snow removal for the parking lot of the édifice Jacinthe-Fyfe is being renewed.

etapes.titre: New snow removal and towing contracts
etapes.texte: City council awards turnkey snow removal contracts for four winter seasons in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest, following the report of the Commission sur l'examen des contrats. It also awards snow-removal-related towing services in Montréal-Nord for three winter seasons.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Léonard indicates that the adoption of its by-law on permits for snow removal contractors is scheduled for September 8, 2026, with notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The extended snow removal equipment rental services in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie begin on November 1, 2026 and continue until March 31, 2027.
The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: The City is awarding contracts to rebuild or rehabilitate water and sewer pipes on streets in several boroughs, and to replace lead service lines, including their portion on private property. It is also funding the continuation of disinfection work at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and awarding construction, monitoring and maintenance contracts there. Loan by-laws govern the financing of these projects.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council increases from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan that finances the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks, and build the oxygen production plant.

The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes using trenchless methods and to redo the roadway on streets in several boroughs. Each contract also includes the replacement of lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild water pipes and infrastructure on rue Guy, between rue Saint-Jacques and boulevard René-Lévesque, and on rue De Champlain, and to rehabilitate a pipe along autoroute 15. It is also adding funds to ongoing contracts, including $12,144,522.14 for the pipe on rue de la Cathédrale leading to the McTavish reservoir.

The City is renewing or awarding contracts to operate the wastewater treatment plant: process control system, chemicals, electrical equipment, sludge incineration systems, fire inspection, and housekeeping.

The urban agglomeration council is awarding a $127,984,000 contract to Construction Deric inc. to build the oxygen production unit, as well as professional services contracts for monitoring this work and for the plant's electrical substation. It is adopting a $12,000,000 loan for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector, and the city council is receiving notice of motion for a $951,000,000 loan for the renewal of secondary networks.

aSurveiller.texte: Commissioning of the ozone plant at the wastewater treatment plant expected in 2029; the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 must be completed in the last quarter of 2028.
Rue Guy project expected from the second quarter of 2026 to December 2027.
Work on the rue de la Cathédrale water pipe extended until March 2027.
Rehabilitation of the pipe along autoroute 15 Nord starting in September 2026, to be completed no later than December 18, 2026.
Leak detection on main pipes from July 2026 to June 2028.
Work on boulevard Gouin Ouest, between rue Des Cageux and rue Coursol, from August 24 to October 15, 2026.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back Park and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned landfill, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, and electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at Frédéric-Back park and the Saint-Michel Environmental Complex: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, modernization of the electrical facilities linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also asking Québec for financial assistance for an east-west pedestrian and bike link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redeveloping rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for assistance of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge about 150 metres long (CG26 0121). The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The agglomeration approves construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Saint-Michel Environmental Complex, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also entrusts two companies with general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough entrusts Groupe MPotvin with the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between Frédéric-Back park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Saint-Michel Environmental Complex, for an additional $296,349.21, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in part for the development of Frédéric-Back park (CG26 0320).

The borough entrusts Les industries Harnois inc. with supplying and installing the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $574,845.80. The project covers two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, flooring, interior partitions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: delivery of the infrastructure in July 2026, work starting in August 2026, and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses commissioning announced for winter 2027.
The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' assistance program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: construction in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to rebuild heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a degraded culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

etapes.titre: Application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques night sky
etapes.texte: The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The submission involves no spending; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, upgrading its fixtures to standards, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, along with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 report on the areas involved.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, road resurfacing, and replacement of the guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected completion of work on the chemin de Senneville stone walls: July 10, 2026.
Submission of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
Response from DarkSky International on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also extending a Ville-Marie public works team dedicated to cleanliness related to homelessness to several boroughs. Lastly, it is setting up a framework to receive private donations for shelter and housing.

etapes.titre: Two buildings lent as warming centres
etapes.texte: The City is lending the former Sainte-Bibiane church, at 5600, 12e Avenue, free of charge to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, for a warming centre for women, for 137 days starting December 15, 2025. It is also lending the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery, at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est, to Projets Autochtones du Québec until April 30, 2026, with a transfer of $97,000 for building costs.

The City is lending the former Bain St-Denis, at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert, to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN for a 90-day warming centre starting February 1, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is extending COHAB inc.'s contract for its 2025-2026 winter warming centre, and Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social for two outreach workers at its facilities.

etapes.titre: Nuit des sans-abri and Notre-Dame encampments
etapes.texte: The City is granting $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal, that is $30,000 per year, for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. It is also awarding a $149,520 contract to Mission Old Brewery to help people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area move toward shelter and housing.

aSurveiller.texte: The public works team's service agreement with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs covers a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary layouts.

etapes.texte: City council amended two leases for land south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent: a 2,787-square-metre lot leased to the Société de transport de Montréal for $49,293 in total, and an 836-square-metre lot leased to a paid parking company for $45,049 before taxes.

The City is extending, free of charge, the loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to an organization that grows a vegetable garden there, and of a 3,316-square-metre lot to an urban agriculture organization for sunflowers and a greenhouse. City council also agreed to prepare itself a free lease of 78,244 square feet, at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, for outreach activities.

etapes.titre: Contract to redevelop rue de Louvain
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes, and authorized total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Outreach and events on the site
etapes.texte: The borough granted $35,000 to an organization to design and run the temporary Esplanade-Louvain space, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, from June 9 to December 31, 2026. It also authorized, on a vacant lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, an event-based and temporary use: multimedia activity, shows, street food, a drink outlet and recreational activities.

etapes.titre: New street, networks and rehabilitated soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded a company a contract of $10,311,940.25 including taxes to build a street with sewer, water main, roadway, lighting and soil management in the eco-district, for total spending of $15,366,336, and added $2,007,312.15 net to rehabilitate the soil of the former gas station area. The borough also adopted a second draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest and the construction of a group of buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The work on rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel takes place in three phases: from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
The loan of the lot for sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2027.
The lease for outreach activities covers two periods from April 1 to October 31, in 2026 and in 2027.
Four other public spaces on the site are still to be named by the end of development, expected around 2032.
The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal starts on October 1, 2026, for three years and a maximum of 92 days per year.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is adjusting its residual materials collections and renewing the contracts that keep them running. It is changing collection days and frequency in several boroughs, buying bins, extending the treatment of food waste and services related to containers and the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It is also tabling the agglomeration's 2025 residual materials management report.

etapes.texte: The executive committee changes collection days, schedules and sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31, and the boundaries of sectors 41 and 42 are revised.

The City extends twice, by six months each time, the composting or biomethanization treatment contracts for food waste awarded to Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. The first extension runs from March 1 to September 30, 2026 and covers about 18,475 tonnes, pending the start-up of the Montréal-Est biomethanization centre.

The City enters into agreements to supply and distribute collection bins to residents, including in Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where garbage collection will be spaced out. Ahuntsic-Cartierville entrusts Ville en vert with an information and awareness service, and Tricentris pays the City $43,773.61 to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Reports tabled and urban planning decisions
etapes.texte: Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Saint-Laurent and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce table their 2025 spending reports, and the urban agglomeration council takes note of the 2025 report and the accountability report of the 2020-2025 Master Plan, which indicates 415 kg of waste per person and 48% of materials diverted from disposal. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal authorizes the development of a waste room at 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest, and Le Sud-Ouest grants a variance for the drop-off area at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest.

The City extends by 12 months the collection of garbage from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the supply and transport of containers for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It awards a contract for the collection and recovery of mattresses and box springs from ecocentres, enters into agreements for studies on former residual materials disposal sites, and extends the dumping authorization management software.

aSurveiller.texte: Collection schedules change on November 1, 2026 in Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where garbage collection is spaced out in two phases, fall 2026 and fall 2027.
The loan of reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until the contribution is used up and no later than December 31, 2026.
Container collection services and container transport for the écocentre Saint-Laurent are maintained until October 31, 2027.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water mains in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Government of Québec grants the City a deadline of October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension comes with no financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a $2,000,000 City guarantee in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects an opposition motion on governance and the management of public assets and funds in the neighbourhood.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and water mains, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build water trunk mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella.

The City leases parcels of the neighbourhood to three organizations for $100 or $200 in rent: temporary urban agriculture with MultiCaf and with the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora, and a transitional tree nursery with the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain.

aSurveiller.texte: The City has until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site.
The federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and redevelopment work of parks in several boroughs, from parc Le Prévost to parc Percy-Walters, often including play areas, water play areas and plantings. Several projects come from Montréal's participatory budget. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, the City is repairing structures, submitting an application for an international designation, and adding a sector to the inventory of protected natural environments.

etapes.titre: Studies and design of new developments
etapes.texte: The City is awarding the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included [CM26 0082]. It is also giving money to Verdun for soil studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard and launching a public art competition for parc des Eaux-Cachées.

etapes.titre: Parc d'Argenson and parc sportif du Sud-Ouest
etapes.texte: Le Sud-Ouest is signing an agreement with Hydro-Québec to obtain $154,000 and carry out phase 4 of parc d'Argenson [CA26 22 0016]. The City is awarding a contract to St-Denis Thompson inc. to develop a sports park between rues Saint-Patrick, Hadley, Roberval and Cabot.

The City is adding money to the contract for the repair of heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and awarding a contract to rebuild a culvert under the same road, at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It is submitting the application of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and adding the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the inventory of protected natural environments.

The City and the boroughs are adjusting contracts already awarded: construction supervision for parc du Bassin-à-Bois, budget transfers for parc des Hirondelles and parc du Sault-au-Récollet, and an additional amount to the architects of parc Denise-Morelle.

City council is removing a 810.2 m² street section from the public domain to add it to parc Campbell Ouest [CM26 0704]. The City is paying $168,472.14 to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension for the environmental remediation of parc George-Vernot and its supervision.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées: selection of the winning public art project in October 2026, contract in December 2026, installation of the artwork in 2028.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a continuation in spring 2027.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work in June 2027.
Cap-Saint-Jacques: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, DarkSky response in April 2027, site compliance in April 2032.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is closing streets to traffic for the summer and funding business development corporations that animate them. Boroughs are adopting ordinances governing these pedestrian streets: schedules, noise, terraces, and food and drink sales. The City is also acting on public squares: development, naming, and changing the designation of a piece of land.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and end of a lawsuit
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street, with applications due by February 16, 2026 at the latest. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer.

The executive committee transfers $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, with each project required to close the street for at least eight consecutive weeks. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN on a ramp of chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges from April 1 to October 31, 2026, and Ville-Marie prohibits traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations.

Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension pays $102,045 to the Société de développement commercial du Quartier Villeray to pedestrianize rue Villeray, between rue Lajeunesse and avenue De Gaspé. Ville-Marie grants $375,500 to the Société de développement commercial du Village for rue Sainte-Catherine Est, and Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard.

Outremont closes avenue Bernard between avenue Bloomfield and the lane east of avenue Wiseman from May 19 to September 24, 2026. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce turns avenue Royal and avenue Madison into public squares from June 1 to October 31, 2026, while Ville-Marie changes the dates of three of its pedestrianizations.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal closes avenue du Mont-Royal and avenue Duluth and awards a $287,724.94 contract to the organization SOCIOCYCLE to transport people with reduced mobility and seniors on request on the pedestrian street. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve closes rue Ontario Est between rue Darling and boulevard Pie-IX and removes paid parking spaces, and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce supports the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal bans amplified instruments on its pedestrian streets and music between 9 p.m. and 8 a.m., while Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a commercial promotion on the closed street on avenue de Monkland and the City pays $40,000 to animate the Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street. City council names a public square in Montréal-Nord "place Chez-Marguerite" and changes the designation of an 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier, which becomes a local park.

aSurveiller.texte: Rue Ontario Est remains closed to cars until September 18, 2026; parking meters return on September 17, 2026.
Avenue Lacombe is closed to cars from September 10 to 13, 2026.
Avenue Bernard fully reopens to traffic on September 25, 2026.
Boroughs funded by the executive committee must report back in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the conformity by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates lodging and service establishments for people in residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration programs. A public assembly was held on March 18, 2026 and a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and site coverage rate in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its conformity by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the plans for view corridors and heights; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and makes certain work subject to approval in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public consultation assembly held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its conformity by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its conformity by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: This year, the City is buying equipment for the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM): motorcycles, pickup trucks, practice ammunition, a patrol boat. It is renewing leases for neighbourhood stations and service premises, extending service contracts (housekeeping, mail, meals for detained persons, software), and lending police officers to the RCMP and the Sûreté du Québec. Some borough councils have also adopted motions of support for the SPVM.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and lending of an officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a $10,880,000 loan to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team on enforcement of the Firearms Act, for three years starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys a port patrol boat with trailer and two 4 x 4 pickup trucks, and assigns to a group of firms the plans, specifications and work supervision for the permanent 9-1-1 relief centre. It accepts a $2,436,490 grant from the ministère de la Sécurité intérieure for the Section spécialisée en violence conjugale and maintains seven police positions and one civilian position linked to this section.

aSurveiller.texte: "Fèves au lard" fundraising day for neighbourhood station 46, supported by the arrondissement d'Anjou, which buys 62 tickets.
Start of the ten-year lease for the premises at 888, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, for the metro unit of neighbourhood station 50, on February 1, 2027.
Expected end of the work to replace the oil heating at the poste de la cavalerie, on September 30, 2027.
Start of the extended lease for the SPVM training centre, rue Ernest-Cormier in Anjou, on November 1, 2033.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and capital program of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) and several of its loan by-laws. It also sells land to the STM for metro facilities, entrusts it with work related to the extension of the blue line, and regulates construction sites and bus stops on its territory.

etapes.texte: The City rents to the STM a 2,787-square-metre piece of land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, used as a parking lot for STM officers' vehicles, for a total rent of $49,293 (CM26 0078). It also buys advertising space in the metro, buses, and the Astral Affichage network for Espace pour la vie, for a maximum of $172,462.50 including taxes.

etapes.titre: Work and areas around the network
etapes.texte: The borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville establishes and removes bus stops as part of the network overhaul. The City signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the metro ventilation station on avenue Wiseman, Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to work day and night in the green line tunnel, and the borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signs an access agreement for a piece of STM land on boulevard Décarie.

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its municipal works at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 including taxes (CG26 0175). It also signs a letter of non-objection for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel over the REM, between rue Jean-Talon Ouest and rue Wilderton, and accepts on loan the archaeological collection from the REM excavations.

The City sells to the STM a 364.3-square-metre piece of land at the Place-Saint-Henri station for $495,150, three pieces of land in Verdun for $257,425 for the Rielle ventilation station, and commits to selling a piece of land of approximately 202.8 square metres on rue Jean-Brillant for $115,000, for a rectifier station. These amounts are understood as plus applicable taxes.

The councils approve STM loan by-laws and amendments to the 2026-2035 capital program, including the bus priority measures program increased to $123,235,302 and Réno-Infrastructures phase 4 increased to $640,000,000. Council grants $382,000 to the STM to strengthen service during the 2026 UCI Road World Championships and adopts a motion on the preservation of the tunnel boring machine "Lisette".

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the parking lot in Ahuntsic-Cartierville runs for three years starting October 1, 2026, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station in Verdun is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays; bridge-tunnel work is planned from June 2026 to March 2028.
According to the blue line extension file, contracts will be awarded in August and October 2026, the City's work is integrated in 2028-2029, and station openings are planned for 2031.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the self-service bike system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docking points and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed as part of street construction projects. It is also funding the repair of existing bike paths, including the REV Lajeunesse, and regularizing rents for Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their own bike paths.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes spending of $100,000, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended in particular for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical works and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 pieces of land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, with total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to lease about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for bike path purposes.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of repairing sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike path works under the Plan Vélo 2019. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contract award in June, and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; sections along the route are targeted by roadway works in Ville-Marie.
Repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
Work on the sustainable mobility corridors resumes in spring 2026, for completion in spring or summer 2026.
